title: Best Angle? Horizontal Range Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A shot put, a long jump and a fielder's throw from the boundary all have one goal: land as far away as possible. Aarav throws a ball at 14 m/s, once at 15 degrees and once at 75. Which one lands farther? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 3, Motion in a Plane) we learn the horizontal range of a projectile.

A live motion notebook launches a ball at 14 m/s and 45 degrees with a readout and a distance-time graph linked to it. A slow-motion replay shows the horizontal velocity never changing, and ghost copies show equal steps across. We derive R = u²sin2θ/g step by step, see the range as the area under the vx-t graph, launch at many angles to find why 45 degrees goes farthest, and compare 20 and 70 degrees side by side with two pause-and-think questions. Then a worked example, the exam trap about the time of flight, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A shot put, a long jump, a fielder's throw: land far
0:27 What is horizontal range? What carries the ball forward
0:51 Live sim: launch at 45°, slow-mo replay, equal steps across
1:33 The formula R = u²sin2θ/g, step by step
2:12 Many angles: why 45° goes farthest + pause and think
2:54 20° vs 70° side by side + pause and think
3:21 Worked example: Aarav's 15° and 75° throws
3:55 Exam trap: use the whole time of flight
4:14 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:55 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Uniform Circular Motion. A mixer jar spins at a steady speed, yet everything inside is accelerating. How?
